comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center Segment serves hyperscale data centers, OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, and independent distributors globally. ODMs provide design and manufacturing services to various resellers and manufacturers.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD identify OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, and distributors as key direct customers in their data center segments. However, NVIDIA explicitly categorizes 'public cloud providers' and 'startups' as end customers in its general customer base summary, while AMD's disclosure for the Data Center Segment specifically highlights 'hyperscale data centers' as a primary customer group alongside the channel partners, and provides additional context that ODMs serve both branded and unbranded resellers.

sentences.text: Our end customers include the world's leading public cloud and consumer internet companies, thousands of enterprises and startups, and public sector entities.

Our direct customers include original equipment manufacturers, or OEMs, original device manufacturers, or ODMs, system integrators and distributors which we partner with to help bring our products to market.

Our Data Center Segment customers consist primarily of hyperscale data centers, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), original design manufacturers (ODMs), system integrators and independent distributors in both domestic and international markets.
ODMs provide design and/or manufacturing services to branded and unbranded private label resellers, OEMs and system builders.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA describes its end customers as including 'world's leading public cloud... companies,' while AMD specifies that 'Large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers directly and indirectly purchase a substantial portion of our data center-focused products.' Both disclosures confirm that major cloud providers are significant end-users, with AMD detailing that these customers incorporate products into servers via OEMs or ODMs.

sentences.text: Our end customers include the world's leading public cloud and consumer internet companies, thousands of enterprises and startups, and public sector entities.

Large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers directly and indirectly purchase a substantial portion of our data center-focused products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SOCs.

These products are incorporated into servers and other data center appliances sold by OEMs to the hyperscale customers or into custom servers or hardware designed by or for these customers and manufactured by ODMs or contract manufacturers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Software customers include large enterprises across various industries, with solutions available directly, through resellers, hyperscale cloud providers, and VMware partners. The company focuses on strengthening relationships with core customer segments and expects its enterprise-wide license model to drive revenue growth by offering reduced complexity and flexibility.
comparisons.comparison: While NVIDIA lists 'public cloud providers' as end customers and AVGO lists 'hyperscale cloud providers' as distribution channels for its software, both companies reference partnerships with cloud providers to reach customers. NVIDIA's disclosure focuses on the broad end-customer base including enterprises and startups, whereas Broadcom's disclosure focuses on large enterprises as its software customer base, noting that solutions are available through hyperscale cloud providers among other channels.

sentences.text: Our end customers include the world's leading public cloud and consumer internet companies, thousands of enterprises and startups, and public sector entities.
We work with industry leaders to help build or transform their applications and data center infrastructure.

Our software customers generally consist of large enterprises that have computing environments from multiple vendors and are in most major industries worldwide, including banks, insurance companies, other financial services providers, government agencies, global IT service providers, telecommunication providers, transportation companies, manufacturers, technology companies, retailers, educational organizations and health care institutions.

Our private cloud infrastructure suite of solutions are available directly from Broadcom, resellers and distributors, hyperscale cloud providers, value-added OEMs and VMware cloud service provider partners.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates focus on Intel's foundry business strategy and co-engineering with software leaders, which do not sufficiently match NVIDIA's disclosure of its end-customer and direct customer base composition in the data center context.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA identifies 'public cloud and consumer internet companies' as end customers driving data center demand. Similarly, Micron states that its data center sales are driven by 'server demand across the cloud and enterprise markets' and 'cloud growth... driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud.' Both disclosures link data center revenue to the cloud computing market, though NVIDIA focuses on the customer identity (providers) while Micron focuses on the demand driver (cloud shift/AI workloads).
